items.difficulty_reason: The lemma compares the categories of sheaves of two sites on the same category: if every covering of the first is tautologically equivalent to one of the second then the sheaves of the second are sheaves for the first, and similarly for refinements, with equality when the comparison holds in both directions (statement lines 1515-1539). The proof is short but complete: part (1) follows directly from the comparison of sheaf conditions under tautological equivalence (proof lines 1542-1543); for part (2) the author chooses a refinement of a given covering in the second site and observes that the sheaf condition holds for that refinement and for the induced coverings, so that the comparison result gives the sheaf condition for the given covering (proof lines 1546-1556). The non-formal content is the choice of refinement and the application of the comparison. The claim is H1: two short arguments, each written out.
